dedupe_keys.name: gasbuddy fuel availability tracker crowdsourced status of gas stations without gasoline diesel or power during disasters north america

description: GasBuddy, a fuel price app that says it covers more than 150,000 gas stations in North America, activates a Fuel Availability Tracker for areas hit by natural disasters and crises, when stations close or run out of fuel or power. When the feature is active, the free app and an online version flag stations reported as having no gasoline, no diesel or no power, highlighting them in red on the map, so drivers can go elsewhere. The status is crowdsourced: motorists report it through a quick report button near a station or by suggesting edits on the station page, and the tracker shows only stations that have been reported. The page, published on 1 June 2025 for the start of the hurricane season, explains the reporting steps. Access is free online and in the iOS and Android apps, but no data download, archive or licence is described on the page read. Coverage is North America where the tracker is activated. Caveats: reports are unverified crowd inputs, coverage depends on how many drivers report, and the tracker only runs during declared events. Simulation uses are observed fuel supply disruption at retail level after hurricanes for calibrating fuel logistics and emergency response models. Related records: data-poweroutage-com-outage-data-products tracks electricity outages in the same events.
